headline: Adopted a resolution authorizing a Tax Increment Financing amendment for 30-36 Washington Sq. and accepted a $7,500 Vest-a-Dog grant for a police canine.
summary: Many traffic and parking requests, including speed humps, stop signs, and handicap spaces, were referred to committee. A Tax Increment Financing amendment for 30-36 Washington Sq. was adopted, along with several finance transfers and authorizations. Public hearings were set for September 22, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. on National Grid conduit locations at Gates St. and Patch St.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 18, 2026 City Council meeting, 11-0.
Referred Keith Boucher's petition for a public report on construction permit and compliance procedures to the City Manager, 11-0.
Referred petitions 7b through 7w, except 7f through 7h, to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Referred the rotary requests and the MassDOT Chandler St. and May St. project pause request to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Set public hearings for September 22, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. on National Grid conduit locations at Gates St. (item 7x) and Patch St. (item 7y), 11-0.
Held Tom Marino's police reform proposal under privilege at the request of Councilor Bilotta.
Adopted a resolution authorizing a Tax Increment Financing Agreement Amendment for 30-36 Washington Sq., 11-0.
Referred the Dog Waste Disposal Advisory to the Public Works Committee, 11-0.
Placed on file the item under 8.11A, the August 2026 street and sidewalk construction progress report, 11-0.
Referred the new speed hump program policies and procedures communication to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Referred Councilor Fresolo's order on street and sidewalk project selection to the Public Works Committee, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor King's motion requesting a report on best practices for street and sidewalk rehabilitation timelines and contractor accountability, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Rivera's motion requesting a detailed process for selecting streets and sidewalks for rehabilitation, 11-0.
Held the public camping ordinance proposal under privilege at the request of Councilor King.
Referred the Opioid Allocation communication to the Public Health and Human Services Committee, 11-0.
Referred the July 2026 Financial Update to the Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 11-0.
Referred the Upcoming DCU Special Tax District Borrowing communication to the Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 11-0.
Adopted a resolution to file, accept, and expend a $7,500.00 grant from Massachusetts Vest-a-Dog, Inc. for a Worcester Police Department canine, 11-0.
Approved finance items 8.36A and 8.37A through 8.37D: a $12,000.00 transfer, authorizations of $24,720.00, $1,794.50, $149.95, and $246,016.27, 11-0.
Referred three City Manager communications on economic development, housing, and TIF/TIE reporting to the Economic Development Committee, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Economou's order requesting a report on winter snow and ice removal preparations, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order requesting a report on converting private streets into public streets, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order requesting a report on keeping private streets passable for public safety vehicles, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order requesting a report on the cost to resurface major arteries, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Rosen's order asking the City Manager to review homelessness response action plans from other cities, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor King's motion requesting a report on how the dissolution of the Central Massachusetts Regional Public Health Alliance affected support for the unhoused population, 11-0.
Adopted, as amended, Councilor Rivera's order on best practices for reporting and acting against spotted lanternflies, 11-0.
Placed Councilor Economou's order on violent incidents near the Worcester Common on file, 10-0, with Councilor Toomey recused.
Granted Councilor Toomey leave to withdraw her order on social service agencies, 10-1, with Councilor Bilotta voting no.
Referred Councilor King's motion on social service agencies working with homeless and addiction treatment programs to the Public Health and Human Services Committee, 10-0.
Adopted Councilor Economou's order requesting repairs to subpar street and sidewalk projects, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order requesting two WooBin trash receptacles on Southbridge St., 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order on sanitation staff driveway turns and debris on city streets, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Bilotta's resolution recognizing September as National Service Dog Month, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order requesting a report on Worcester Police Department SMART goals and accountability, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Ojeda's order requesting a report on the increase in arrests over five years, 11-0.
Referred Councilor King's order on joint meetings with the School Committee's Standing Committee on Operations and Governance to the Education Committee, 10-0.
Denied Councilor King's motion to hold an Executive Session on improper conduct of a Worcester Police Officer, 4-6, and denied reconsideration, 1-9.
Adopted Councilor King's motion requesting a report from the Mayor on Rules 48 and 49 on committee and temporary appointments, 10-0, with Councilor Toomey recused.

7. PETITIONS
7a. Keith Boucher request a public report be written regarding the city’s procedures for 
ensuring that zoning conditions, permit prerequisites, approved plans, and other required 
regulatory approvals are satisfied before construction is authorized to proceed, and for 
monitoring compliance after work begins. Said report should address how 
responsibilities are coordinated among departments when multiple municipal approvals 
apply to the same project; how outstanding conditions and requirements are tracked and 
verified before subsequent stages of construction are authorized; how Stop Work orders 
and other corrective actions are monitored through resolution; and how material 
compliance concerns reported by residents are reviewed, documented, and 
communicated. Further, request that the administration identify any procedural or 
coordination improvements that may strengthen consistent enforcement, accountability, 
and public confidence in the city’s development and construction oversight process.
